newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kashmiri hostage relatives appeal for release.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri hostage relatives appeal for release.

text.p: Relatives of three of four Western hostages held by Kashmiri separatists for more than 15 months appealed to the people of Pakistani Azad (free) Kashmir on Friday to help secure their release.

Julie Mangan, wife of Briton Keith Mangan, told a news conference her husband and his fellow captives in the hands of the shadowy Al-Faran group should be released if alive. If not, their bodies should be handed back to their families.
"We are very worried and fearful for their safety and have been for the past 487 days," the relatives said in a joint appeal.
"Please put an end to our worries. Please help us to secure their release and allow them to rejoin their families in England, America and Germany."
Americans Donald Hutchings and John Childs and Britons Mangan and Paul Wells were kidnapped on July 4, 1995, while trekking in Kashmir.
Four days later, Childs escaped and German Dirk Hasert and Norwegian Hans Christian Ostroe were captured by the same guerrillas. Ostroe was beheaded in August.

"We ask for information about our husbands and dear ones and we will continue to ask as we know that there are people in India and we believe there are people in Pakistan who know the answer," said Hutchings's wife, Jane Schelly.

Al-Faran had not been heard of before the kidnappings. Dozens of guerrilla groups are fighting Indian rule over Jammu and Kashmir state. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in the six-year-old revolt.
India controls two-thirds and Pakistan one-third of Kashmir, over which the two countries have fought two wars since independence from Britain in 1947.
